How do you carry a batch of scalar detector chromatograms from a raw file to
reported concentrations with full provenance, QC verification, and explicit
flags for missing, interfered, and out-of-range injections? This guide walks
through one 13-injection externally calibrated HPLC-UV numerical control batch
included with the package.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(measure)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Read the batch file and manifest

The control batch (`lc_batch_control.csv`) contains 13 injections on a single
UV 254 nm channel (`3.00` to `7.50` min at `0.02` min spacing, 226 points per
injection). Every injection includes a sloping baseline and an unrelated matrix
peak near `3.70` min outside the declared analyte retention window
`[4.8, 5.6]` min.

`read_measure_record_delim()` reads the raw CSV bytes once, records the file's
SHA-256 digest, and retains the exact parsed row ordinal (`.source_rows`) for
every chromatogram point.

```{r load}
data_path <- system.file(
  "extdata",
  "lc_batch_control.csv",
  package = "measure",
  mustWork = TRUE
)
manifest_path <- system.file(
  "extdata",
  "lc_batch_manifest.csv",
  package = "measure",
  mustWork = TRUE
)

columns <- c(
  sample_id = "sample_id",
  injection_id = "injection_id",
  channel_id = "channel_id",
  channel_name = "channel_name",
  curve_id = "curve_id",
  axis_name = "axis_name",
  axis_unit = "axis_unit",
  value_name = "value_name",
  value_unit = "value_unit",
  location = "location",
  value = "value"
)

record <- read_measure_record_delim(
  data_path,
  columns = columns,
  source_id = "lc-batch-control"
)
expected_sha256 <- "8a9f439a1e4c413d0e6abc138ff8bc26e36282d2210a7f0573c116c3e8769949"
stopifnot(identical(record$sources$source_sha256[[1]], expected_sha256))

manifest <- utils::read.csv(manifest_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
manifest
```

The manifest declares:

- **Blank (`INJ-01`)**: zero analyte; checked against a blank ceiling of 20% of
  the fitted LLOQ response.
- **Standards (`INJ-02` to `INJ-06`)**: five calibration levels spanning `5` to
  `100` mg/L (`cal-control-v1`).
- **QC injections (`INJ-07`, `INJ-08`)**: low QC (`15` mg/L, passing within
  ±15%) and high QC (`60` mg/L, intentionally biased +22% to exercise QC failure).
- **Unknowns (`INJ-09` to `INJ-13`)**: an undiluted in-range sample (~35 mg/L),
  a 2x diluted sample (~40 mg/L in vial, ~80 mg/L reported), an above-ULOQ
  sample (~135 mg/L), a missing-peak sample (non-detect), and an interfered
  sample with two resolved peaks inside `[4.8, 5.6]` min.

## Run peak integration, calibration, and QC

`measure_quantify_batch()` extracts the curves via `measure_record_curves()`,
runs `step_measure_peaks_detect()` (prominence ≥ 1.0 mAU) and
`step_measure_peaks_integrate()` (trapezoidal area above a local linear
baseline clamped at zero), fits unweighted linear regression
`area ~ nominal_conc` via `measure_calibration_fit()`, checks in-vial
concentrations against `[5, 100]` mg/L before applying `dilution_factor`, and
verifies QC injections via `measure_calibration_verify()`.

```{r quantify}
batch <- measure_quantify_batch(
  record = record,
  manifest = manifest,
  window = c(4.8, 5.6),
  analyte = "caffeine_control",
  conc_unit = "mg/L",
  calibration_revision = "cal-control-v1",
  min_prominence = 1.0,
  integration_method = "trapezoid",
  baseline = "local",
  model = "linear",
  weights = "none",
  qc_acceptance_pct = 15,
  blank_max_pct_lloq = 20
)
batch
```

Every row in `summary(batch)` carries the injection identity, peak bounds,
integrated area, calibration revision, estimated in-vial concentration,
dilution-adjusted reported concentration, outcome, QC status, and exact CSV
source-row bounds for both the chromatogram and the integrated peak.

```{r table}
res <- summary(batch)
res |>
  select(
    injection_id,
    sample_id,
    injection_type,
    peak_count,
    area,
    calibration_revision,
    dilution_factor,
    estimated_conc,
    reported_conc,
    outcome,
    qc_status,
    peak_source_row_start,
    peak_source_row_end
  )
```

Notice how failure modes stay explicit rather than collapsing into valid zeros
or silently extrapolated values:

- `INJ-08` (`QC-HIGH`) fails QC (`outcome = "qc_fail"`, `qc_status = "fail"`),
  and `batch$verification` reports `overall_pass = FALSE`.
- `INJ-11` (`UNK-03`) retains its raw in-vial estimate (`134.91` mg/L) for
  diagnostics while leaving `reported_conc = NA` with `outcome = "above_uloq"`.
- `INJ-12` (`UNK-04`) reports `outcome = "missing_peak"` with `area = NA` and
  `reported_conc = NA`.
- `INJ-13` (`UNK-05`) detects two peaks inside `[4.8, 5.6]` min and reports
  `outcome = "interfered_peak"` rather than silently selecting one.

## Inspect chromatograms and calibration

```{r plots, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5, fig.alt="Batch UV chromatograms faceted by injection type with the 4.8 to 5.6 minute analyte retention window shaded."}
autoplot(batch, type = "chromatograms")
```

```{r cal-plot, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4, fig.alt="External linear calibration curve showing the five standards and overlaid QC and unknown responses."}
autoplot(batch, type = "calibration")
```

## Compare with an independent calculation

Before running the comparison, we declare tolerances of `1e-9 mAU·min` for peak
areas and calibration parameters, `1e-9 mg/L` for estimated and reported
concentrations, and exact agreement on file SHA-256, peak counts, outcomes, QC
flags, and peak source-row spans.

An independent standard-library Python script reads `lc_batch_control.csv` and
`lc_batch_manifest.csv` directly from raw bytes and reproduces every quantity.
[Independent Python reference](https://github.com/JamesHWade/measure/blob/main/tools/chromatography/batch-reference.py)

```{r verify}
tol <- 1e-9
coefs <- stats::coef(batch$calibration$model)
stopifnot(
  abs(unname(coefs[[1]]) - 0.5686644570673636) < tol,
  abs(unname(coefs[[2]]) - 1.4511419544975344) < tol,
  abs(res$area[[2]] - 7.878024541962506) < tol,
  abs(res$reported_conc[[9]] - 34.99324700912393) < tol,
  abs(res$reported_conc[[10]] - 79.97846280752921) < tol,
  is.na(res$reported_conc[[11]]),
  identical(res$outcome[[11]], "above_uloq"),
  identical(res$outcome[[12]], "missing_peak"),
  identical(res$outcome[[13]], "interfered_peak")
)
```

## Export a standalone report

`measure_batch_results` implements `measure_report_sections()`, so
`render_measure_report()` packages the method provenance, quantitation table,
calibration plot, and chromatograms directly:

```{r report, eval=FALSE}
render_measure_report(
  batch,
  "lc-batch-control-report.html",
  title = "External Calibration Batch Control (cal-control-v1)",
  open = FALSE
)
```

## Limitations and package boundary

- **Constructed control fixture**: `lc_batch_control.csv` is an explicitly
  constructed Gaussian-plus-baseline numerical control. It qualifies the
  end-to-end record, integration, calibration, dilution, and flagging
  arithmetic, while measured-method qualification on real instrument data stays
  open in issue #84.
- **Core vs. optional `measure.lc` pack**: Core `measure` already provides the
  scalar relational record (`measure_record`, `read_measure_record_delim`,
  `measure_record_curves`), peak detection/integration, calibration fitting and
  verification, single-analyte batch quantitation (`measure_quantify_batch`),
  and report export. Technique-specific capabilities—multi-analyte target
  libraries, internal-standard response-factor matrices, vendor chromatogram
  format adapters, DAD spectral deconvolution, and USP/EP chromatographic
  system-suitability conventions—belong in an optional `measure.lc` technique
  pack rather than core.
